subject.title: Cron Jobs Calendar View for Control UI

question: Should OpenClaw accept a repaired 24-hour Cron Jobs timeline as the first Control UI slice, or require a fuller daily/week calendar and editing design before implementation?
rationale: The request is a new Control UI product surface, the current linked PR only covers part of the requested scope, and automation should not open a competing fix PR while that product direction and linked PR remain open.

options.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
options.body: Rebase the linked PR onto `ui/src/pages/cron/*`, keep current cron contracts, and accept the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting broader day/week/editing scope separately.

options.title: Design Full Calendar Scope
options.body: Pause the linked PR until maintainers define the daily, weekly, stats, drag-and-drop, and validation behavior as one coherent Control UI design.

options.title: Decline Core Calendar View
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR after documenting that the existing list/run-history UI is sufficient for core for now.

recommendation.title: Repair Narrow Timeline First
recommendation.body: Rebase the linked PR onto `ui/src/pages/cron/*`, keep current cron contracts, and accept the 24-hour timeline as an intentional first slice while tracking or rejecting broader day/week/editing scope separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Control UI product-scope choice, and recent Control UI docs plus cron editor history make this the best available routing signal.
